title: Observability: refine token-level KV metrics, tracing, dashboards and alert tuning
author: Ava Chen
body:
Motivation: Improve visibility into token-level KV cache behavior and per-token cost/latency breakdowns so platform engineers and SREs can quickly identify regressions (cache miss storms, query-level hotspots) and tune alerts with lower false-positive rates. This PR implements metric and tracing refinements, updates dashboards, and adjusts alert thresholds based on recent load tests and production signals.

What changed (high level): 1) Add new Prometheus metrics: redwood_kv_token_request_total (labelled by model, route, outcome), redwood_kv_token_cache_miss_ratio (windowed), redwood_token_unit_cost_estimated; 2) Emit token-level tracing spans and attach kv_hit/kb_size tags to the request span to correlate latency with cache behavior; 3) Grafana dashboard updates: new per-route token cost/latency panels, KV hit-ratio heatmap, and correlation panels that join span durations to cache miss ratio; 4) Alert tuning: reduce sensitivity on p99 token latency alerts by requiring sustained increase + elevated KV miss ratio; add a low-severity alert for sudden KV miss-rate spikes (>=10% delta sustained 5m) and a medium-severity alert when both P95 latency and miss-rate increase; 5) Docs: observability runbook updates and dashboard walkthrough.

Testing and verification: Unit tests added for metrics aggregation logic and tag consistency. Integration test simulates cache warm/cold scenarios and asserts metrics and spans are emitted with expected labels. Load testing on perf-canary showed a ~12% improvement in alert precision (fewer false-positives) when using the tuned rules. CI: initial lint/format failure fixed in second commit, full test suite and telemetry e2e smoke passed.

Rollout plan: feature-flag telemetry changes (opt-in for the first week) with automatic rollout to all regions after monitoring. Dashboard changes are additive; alert rule changes will be staged to 'staging' first then promoted. Runbook includes steps to rollback to previous alert set and metric names if needed.

Notes: Metric names intentionally include route and model labels to avoid ambiguous aggregation. Kept cardinality conservative by limiting label values and using table-driven label whitelists. See linked linear tickets for follow-ups on TTL-based sampling and longer retention for token-level metrics.
commits: a1b2c3d: add redwood_kv_token cache metrics and aggregation window
d4e5f6a: emit token-level tracing spans and attach kv_hit/kb_size tags
b7c8d9e: grafana: add token-KV heatmap and cost/latency correlation panels
c0d1e2f: alerts: tune p99/p95 latency alerts to require sustained increase + miss-rate condition
e3f4a5b: docs: observability runbook and dashboard walkthrough
review_comments: Diego Martinez: Please confirm metric cardinality limits and that model/route labels are whitelisted to avoid high cardinality. Also suggest a smaller default window for miss_ratio to surface short bursts.
Ava Chen: Addressed in commit d4e5f6a and added labels_whitelist.go with conservative defaults. Miss ratio window reduced from 10m to 5m and made configurable via env var.
Priya Singh: The alert pairing looks better but we should ensure alerts don't flappy on deploys — add a 10m for the sustained condition or require >2 evaluation cycles.
Ava Chen: Updated alert rules to require 5m sustained for a 2-of-3 evaluation cycle in token_kv_alerts.yaml. Added notes in runbook about deployment flapping and suggested silence steps.
Liam O'Connor: Can you add an e2e smoke to validate spans show kv_hit tag for both cache-hit and miss paths?
Ava Chen: Added tests/integration/test_token_kv_metrics.py to assert span tags in smoke scenario. CI now verifies this.
Priya Singh: Approved after the alert tuning changes look reasonable in staging graphs.
ci_checks: ci/lint: failed on first run (formatting in telemetry/metrics/token_kv_metrics.go) — fixed in commit f6a7b8c
ci/e2e: passed on perf-canary (load test comparison for alert precision)
release_notes: Improved token-level observability: added KV cache and token cost metrics, token-level tracing span tags, updated Grafana dashboards for per-route cost/latency correlation, and tuned alerts to reduce false positives. Backwards-compatible metric additions; no breaking changes.
additional_notes: Feature gated telemetry flag 'telemetry.token_kv_details' enabled for rollout
Follow-ups: ENG-3589 implement TTL-based sampling for long-term retention, ENG-3421 explore lower-overhead span sampling for high-traffic routes
